masteryModel.contentStrategy: reviewed canonical lesson + quiz bank backbone; Claude supplies adaptive diagnosis, re-teaching, fresh items, and Q&A

concepts.name: What SDM is
concepts.objective: Explain that SDM maintains supplemental data in DDH — the extra attributes downstream apps need that the source systems don't provide, layered onto the imported system-of-record data — and is the human, RACI self-serve editor for the CSSD-curated portion of DDH, where people make the authoritative edits the Sync-* fleet then propagates.
concepts.remediationAngle: Two anchors: (1) 'supplemental' — SDM maintains, in DDH, the attributes the source systems don't provide (plus the sync config); the data lives in DDH, SDM is the editor; (2) RACI self-serve — the data owners edit their own data. Contrast with the mechanical Sync-* fleet that just propagates the result.

concepts.name: How SDM is built (two repos, one app)
concepts.objective: Describe SDM as one deployed web app from two repos: an Angular SPA served at /Iapetus plus an ASP.NET Core 8 backend (REST /api/* and SPA host) over the SchoolObjectModel SQL database via EF Core.
concepts.remediationAngle: Trace a single request: browser asks for /Iapetus (SPA shell) or /api/* (JSON) -> ASP.NET Core backend -> EF Core -> SchoolObjectModel DB.

concepts.name: Authorization via AAD groups
concepts.objective: Explain that SDM authorizes in two layers: the menu options are made available from the user's Entra (AAD) DA-* group claims on the OIDC token (a 403 = a missing group), and the data on the screens is then filtered by the Permission tables in DDH's 'Security' schema (the full RACI-applied access). DA-* group memberships can be managed in SDM via the Standalone Group menu (e.g. Help-Desk temporary access), taking effect at the user's next sign-in.
concepts.remediationAngle: Two layers: (1) menu from DA-* claims — trace one sign-in (Entra OIDC -> DA-* claims -> menu + API check -> 200/403), and note those memberships are managed in SDM via Standalone Groups (Help-Desk temp access), reaching the user at next sign-in; (2) screen data filtered by the Permission tables in DDH's 'Security' schema (RACI) — so an accessible screen with thin/absent data is this layer, not a missing group.

concepts.name: The core domain entities
concepts.objective: Name the main things SDM manages — Schools, Staff (and jobs), the three Data-Owner security groups, Standalone Groups, the org structures (Municipal Divisions, District Programs, Wards, Trustee Positions), and Site Security — and that edits write to DDH with CreatedBy/UpdatedBy audit.
concepts.remediationAngle: Group the nouns: people (Staff, Vendor Reps), org structure (Schools, Municipal Divisions, Wards, District Programs, Trustee Positions), and access (Data Owners, Standalone Groups, Site Security).

concepts.name: Two front ends: the legacy shell and the Iapetus app
concepts.objective: Explain that SDM serves two front ends from one backend — a legacy AngularJS shell that renders the menu/outer page and a newer Angular SPA mounted at /Iapetus — and that each nav link is either an in-app /Iapetus route (upgraded) or a legacy link.
concepts.remediationAngle: Follow a click: the legacy Razor shell (HomeController/IapetusController) renders the page + menu; an 'upgraded' link loads the Angular SPA at /Iapetus/<feature>, while a legacy link stays in the AngularJS shell.

concepts.name: How the menu is built (management tasks)
concepts.objective: Describe how SDM builds each user's menu: their DA-* AAD group claims map (via SQL) to 'management tasks', and a nav link only appears when the user holds the task that grants it — so the menu is per-user.
concepts.remediationAngle: Chain it: DA-* groups -> a stored proc maps groups to management tasks -> NavigationLinkService emits only the links whose task the user holds; the Training link is the exception (always shown, config-driven).

concepts.name: Editing the record: audit and soft-delete
concepts.objective: State that every SDM edit writes to DDH on entities with a GUID Id, CreatedBy/UpdatedBy audit fields, and a soft-delete flag, with an AuditLog row per change — so changes are attributable and reversible, and DDH (not SDM) holds the data.
concepts.remediationAngle: An edit is never a silent overwrite: the entity carries a GUID Id + CreatedBy/UpdatedBy + a soft-delete flag, and an AuditLog row records who/what/when — all in DDH.

concepts.name: Notifications and the temp-job workflow
concepts.objective: Explain that SDM sends email notifications (via the shared Cssd.IT.EmailNotifications / MailKit library) for events like on-hold / temp-job merges — config-driven and disabled in dev — and that this covers HR-gap staffing (temp jobs under six weeks, contractors, vendors) SDM exists to manage.
concepts.remediationAngle: Tie it to purpose: SDM owns the HR-gap staffing (temp jobs under six weeks, contractors, vendors); creating/merging those can fire a config-driven email that is off in dev via DisableEmailNotifications.

concepts.name: Managing Schools
concepts.objective: Use the Schools page to augment school records imported from the HRAD system of record (SDM never creates or deletes schools) — maintaining the supplemental attributes downstream systems need and linking Attendance Area maps, District Programs, and Municipal Divisions to the school.
concepts.remediationAngle: Schools come from HRAD via the syncs; SDM only augments them. The page's job is supplemental attributes plus linking the school to Attendance Areas, District Programs, and Municipal Divisions.

concepts.name: Data Owners and delegates
concepts.objective: Explain how a manager (Department), principal (School), or owner (Functional Site) assigns a delegate to maintain that area's supplemental data and to manage its SharePoint Online site — SDM's RACI self-serve model, where responsibility sits with the owner or their delegate, not a central team.
concepts.remediationAngle: Same feature, three scopes (Department/School/Functional Site): the owner delegates editorial + SPO-site management. It's the RACI self-serve model in action.

concepts.name: Standalone Groups (rules, staff, DA-* linkage)
concepts.objective: Use Standalone Groups to add staff by HR-attribute rules or directly with start/end dates, view a group's membership, and link a group to a DA-* AAD group — functionality being ported from the old config JSON; SDM owns these groups (it can create and delete them).
concepts.remediationAngle: Two ways to populate a standalone group — HR-attribute rules or direct staff add (with start/end) — plus optional linkage to a DA-* group; this was lifted out of the config JSON and SDM owns the groups outright.

concepts.name: Requesting a Subsite
concepts.objective: Explain that SDM offers a subsite request (because the highest SPO permission delegated is 'Contribute', which can't create a subsite) and that the requested subsite is created the next time the SharePoint Online sync runs.
concepts.remediationAngle: You can't create a subsite directly (Contribute is the ceiling), so SDM records a request that the SPO sync fulfils on its next run.

concepts.name: Managing Staff (FTE vs Contractor)
concepts.objective: Distinguish augmenting FTE staff (loaded from the HR system of record) from fully maintaining Contractors (paid or volunteer — security account/email, initial jobs linked to the manager); use Staff augmentation (Service Area, Support Languages, Proxy Addresses), user-account changes, FTE↔Contractor conversion, and the On-Hold name-conflict resolution for new FTEs.
concepts.remediationAngle: FTEs are augmented (they come from HR); Contractors are fully maintained in SDM (account/email, initial job, manager). Both get the same access relative to their manager. Know the extras: account changes, FTE↔Contractor conversion, and On-Hold for name conflicts.

concepts.name: School Staff on external sites
concepts.objective: Use School Staff to manage the HR-sourced staff information shown on external school sites — applying school-friendly job labels and privacy values, with bulk features to reset values at the start of each school year.
concepts.remediationAngle: This page governs what the public school site shows about HR-sourced staff: friendly job labels + privacy values, with a start-of-year bulk reset.

concepts.name: Vendor Representatives
concepts.objective: Explain that Vendor Reps are representatives of 3rd-party suppliers SDM owns because HR doesn't manage them — they receive a login account and a matching CSSD email but no other access to CSSD assets.
concepts.remediationAngle: Vendor Reps are an HR-gap category SDM creates and maintains; give them a login + CSSD email, but nothing beyond that — no broader CSSD access.

concepts.name: School Job Assignment
concepts.objective: Explain that principals or their delegates assign staff at their school to temporary jobs chosen from a canned list of jobs.
concepts.remediationAngle: Scoped to a school: the principal (or delegate) assigns staff to temporary jobs picked from a predefined list — distinct from the district-wide Temporary Job Assignment page.

concepts.name: Temporary Job Assignment
concepts.objective: Use Temporary Job Assignment for the HR-gap temporary jobs (under six weeks) SDM owns and creates directly, and for maintaining Contractor job changes.
concepts.remediationAngle: Temp jobs under six weeks are HR-gap staffing SDM creates; this page also handles Contractor job changes. Tie back to S2.4's notifications.

concepts.name: Municipal Divisions and hierarchy
concepts.objective: Maintain the city-provided set of communities/quadrants/cities that schools service, and the parent/child hierarchy (communities rolling up into quadrants and cities), including the link associating the communities a school services.
concepts.remediationAngle: Two related pages: the divisions themselves (city-provided communities/quadrants/cities) and their hierarchy (what rolls up into what), with a link to the communities a school services.

concepts.name: District Programs
concepts.objective: Maintain the district programs offered by the district and link programs to the schools that provide them.
concepts.remediationAngle: Maintain the catalog of district programs and associate each with the schools offering it.

concepts.name: Trustees and Wards
concepts.objective: Maintain the 7 elected trustees with their position and boundary maps, and the wards related to each trustee — data used for the external district site.
concepts.remediationAngle: Seven elected trustees, each with a position + boundary map; wards relate to a trustee. This data feeds the external district site.

concepts.name: Team Site Security
concepts.objective: Review and maintain team site security, viewing the per-site access matrix either by asset (which users can access a site) or by user (which sites a user can access).
concepts.remediationAngle: Same underlying access matrix, two lenses: by asset (start from a site, see its users) or by user (start from a person, see their sites).
